text_to_speech: Hello astronomers! When we search for a low light polluted sky, we usually we haven’t any power outlet readily available when we have to move with our telescope. And since a modern astrophotography telescope is composed of many devices that might require considerable power, choosing the correct battery is critical in order to allow us to use our telescope all night long! “All night looooong……” Thanks to the EAGLE’s distribution of power to your 12V devices, you will just need a single battery to power your entire telescope. So you can build a field battery yourself or you can search for a battery system to buy. We got in contact with EcoFlow, a company specialized in high capacity, portable, lightweight power stations and we tested their line of smart batteries called “RIVER” to see if they can improve your EAGLE-powered telescope’s portability! RIVER is a portable power station that integrates high capacity lithium batteries so they’re more compact and lightweight than a standard deep-cycle 12V battery of a comparable capacity. You might be asking yourself “Why does PrimaLuceLab recommend this battery above the others on the market?” Our recommendation is based on the cigarette plug power out port they offer. It's not simply rated 12V but, in reality, it’s 13.3V and this is the perfect solution to plug the power cable included with the EAGLE. In fact, because of the architecture of the power distribution in the EAGLE, when you power many devices you have to take into consideration a small voltage drop that slightly reduces the final voltage at the power out ports. For example, if you connect your EAGLE to a battery with an output of exactly 12V, and your EAGLE has to power many devices, the voltage at power out ports of the EAGLE may end up lower than 12V. And, if the voltage drops lower than 11.6v, the EAGLE will automatically shut down and disconnect power for safety. That’s why the optional AC power adapter for the EAGLE is rated at 12.8v. If you want to run off of a battery, it’s critical to have a voltage higher than 12V. This makes the 13.3v of output from the cigarette power port of the RIVER a perfect match for our EAGLE-powered telescope. Let me show you: when I turn on the power ports in the EAGLE Manager and I activate camera cooling, you can see that the voltage of the EAGLE remains above 12V. And, since the RIVER uses lithium batteries, the voltage is very stable until battery is fully discharged so your astrophotography setup will correctly work for the entire battery lifetime. Another useful feature for astrophotography is the projected battery lifetime based on real-time power consumption, you can read on the front panel of the RIVER power station. Of course you can compare this with the power consumption data available in the EAGLE Manager but the display allows you to have a quick look of the battery status even without having to be connected to your remote desktop connection. Here at PrimaLuceLab, we tested the RIVER model with 288Wh capacity that, by considering a telescope with around 5A power consumption, should allow around 4.5 hours of lifetime. It weights 5.3kg. The larger RIVER PRO model with 720Wh capacity allows around 10.5 hours of lifetime with the same telescope power consumption. It weights 7.3kg. Both batteries are able to improve your telescope portability so it’s a perfect match to your EAGLE-powered astrophotography setup! For more content that will help you to explore the Universe like a pro, subscribe to our channel and…. clear skies!

youtube_description:
Choosing the correct battery for a complete telescope is critical since, usually, astrophotography setups are composed by many devices that need to be powered all night long. And when use an EAGLE-powered telescope, all the devices (cameras, mount, focuser, rotator, etc) are connected to the power out ports of the EAGLE and powered through it, so you need just one power source. But the battery you choose has to provide the correct power and has to provide the right capacity for the needed lifetime. Since there are many in the market, astrophotographers often ask us which one to buy. In this article we'll show you EcoFlow RIVER and explain why this is the battery we suggest for EAGLE-powered telescopes! Please note: tested battery is the EcoFlow RIVER available in 2021 and 2022, later models have not been tested.

Read the article: https://www.primalucelab.com/blog/support/the-battery-we-suggest-for-your-eagle-powered-telescope/

Where to buy: https://www.ilportaledelsole.it/1054-power-station
